source_evidence.observation: The paper frames the underlying problem as computing the sum of n floating-point numbers.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (1.2) and the paragraph immediately following it
source_evidence.observation: The standard model uses unit roundoff u and fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for op in {+, -, *, /}; the paper explicitly assumes that no floating-point underflows occur.

source_evidence.anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph, recursive-summation pseudocode, definition of E_n, and equation (2.1)
source_evidence.observation: The data are written as real numbers x_1,...,x_n; S_n = sum_{i=1}^n x_i is the exact sum, S_hat_n is the recursively computed sum, E_n = S_hat_n - S_n, and the standard recursion uses S_hat_k = fl(S_hat_{k-1} + x_k) for k = 2,...,n.
The convention is product_{i=1}^m (1 + delta_i) = 1 + theta_m with |theta_m| <= gamma_m := m u/(1 - m u).
Under the standard model, the paper gives an order-dependent gamma-bound and the weaker bound |E_n| <= gamma_{n-1} sum_{i=1}^n |x_i| = (n - 1)u sum_{i=1}^n |x_i| + O(u^2).
Under the standard model, E_n is expressed through local relative errors and bounded by u/(1-u) times sum_{k=2}^n |S_hat_k|.
The paper emphasizes that (2.8) uses computed partial sums while excluding S_hat_1 = x_1 and does not contain the individual terms x_i.
For machines without a guard digit in addition, the standard model is replaced by fl(x +/- y) = x(1 + alpha) +/- y(1 + beta), with |alpha|, |beta| <= u and the same choice of sign on both sides.
The paper says that equation (2.4) remains valid after replacing (x_1 + x_2)theta_{n-1} by x_1 theta_{n-1} + x_2 theta'_{n-1}, and consequently equations (2.5) and (2.6) are unchanged.
The displayed equation literally reads E_n = sum_{k=2}^n (S_hat_{k-1} alpha_k + x_i beta_k), |alpha_k|, |beta_k| <= u. The index i in x_i is not bound by the displayed summation.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (5.3) and the immediately following sentence
source_evidence.observation: The paper gives |E_n| <= u sum_{k=2}^n (|S_hat_{k-1}| + |x_k|), followed by the looser bound 3u sum_{k=1}^n |S_hat_k| + O(u^2).
The paper explicitly notes that (5.3) contains S_hat_1 = x_1, unlike (2.8).

binders: n is the number of summands in the finite sequence x_1,...,x_n; the local-error formulas use k = 2,...,n. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: Section 2 opening and equation (2.1)]

x_1,...,x_n are called real numbers in Section 2, while the abstract describes the inputs as floating-point numbers. [PDF page 1 (printed 783), anchor: Abstract; PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: Section 2 opening]
u denotes the unit roundoff. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: sentence introducing equation (1.2)]

Equation (5.1) introduces alpha and beta with |alpha|, |beta| <= u; equation (5.2) uses step-indexed alpha_k and beta_k. Neither display writes formal quantifiers. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.1) and (5.2)]
The summation index in equation (5.2) is k, but its second local-error term is printed as x_i beta_k; i is unbound there. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.2)]
hypotheses: The arithmetic lacks a guard digit in addition and is modeled by the componentwise addition/subtraction relation (5.1). [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: Section 5 opening and equation (5.1)]
Every relevant componentwise error magnitude is bounded by the unit roundoff u. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.1) and (5.2)]
No floating-point underflows occur. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: paragraph immediately after equation (1.2)]
The computed result is produced by standard recursive summation in the listed order, beginning with s = 0. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: recursive-summation pseudocode and equation (2.1)]
conclusions: Explicit literal equation (5.2): E_n = sum_{k=2}^n (S_hat_{k-1} alpha_k + x_i beta_k), with |alpha_k|, |beta_k| <= u; the displayed x_i has an unbound index. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.2)]

Inferred intended local-error identity: applying (5.1) at recursive step k and telescoping gives E_n = sum_{k=2}^n (S_hat_{k-1} alpha_k + x_k beta_k). This x_k version is an inference, not a printed correction. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: equation (2.1); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.1)-(5.3)]
Explicit equation (5.3): |E_n| <= u sum_{k=2}^n (|S_hat_{k-1}| + |x_k|). [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3)]
The right-hand side of (5.3) is further bounded by 3u sum_{k=1}^n |S_hat_k| + O(u^2). [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: sentence immediately after equation (5.3)]

In the cross-referenced expansion (2.4), the term (x_1 + x_2)theta_{n-1} is replaced by x_1 theta_{n-1} + x_2 theta'_{n-1}. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: paragraph between equations (5.1) and (5.2)]

The order-dependent bound (2.5) remains |E_n| <= (|x_1| + |x_2|)gamma_{n-1} + sum_{i=3}^n |x_i|gamma_{n-i+1}. [PDF page 3 (printed 785), anchor: equation (2.5); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: paragraph between equations (5.1) and (5.2)]

The order-independent bound (2.6) remains |E_n| <= gamma_{n-1} sum_{i=1}^n |x_i| = (n - 1)u sum_{i=1}^n |x_i| + O(u^2). [PDF page 3 (printed 785), anchor: equation (2.6); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: paragraph between equations (5.1) and (5.2)]
definitions_and_conventions: S_n := sum_{i=1}^n x_i is the exact mathematical sum, S_hat_n is the floating-point result of recursive summation, and E_n := S_hat_n - S_n is the signed forward error. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: Section 2 opening and definition of E_n]

S_hat_k denotes the computed prefix after processing x_1,...,x_k; the analysis uses S_hat_1 = x_1. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: equation (2.1); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: sentence beginning 'Notice that (5.3)']
fl denotes the result of a floating-point arithmetic operation. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: equation (1.2)]
The theta convention is |theta_m| <= gamma_m with gamma_m := m u/(1 - m u). [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: product simplification immediately after equation (2.2)]
The +/- notation in (5.1) couples the sign: addition uses plus on both sides and subtraction uses minus on both sides. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.1)]
implicit_context: The definitions of S_n, S_hat_n, E_n, and recursive summation are inherited from Section 2 rather than restated in Section 5. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: Section 2 opening; PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: sentence introducing the use of (5.1) in place of (1.2)]
The result is scalar: each x_i, prefix sum, and error is a scalar quantity. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: Section 2 opening and equations (2.1)-(2.2)]
The analysis initially makes no assumption on the ordering of the x_i; the formulas apply to their listed recursive order. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: paragraph before equation (2.1)]

The componentwise recurrence S_hat_k = S_hat_{k-1}(1 + alpha_k) + x_k(1 + beta_k) is inferred by applying (5.1) to the kth recursive addition. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: equation (2.1); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.1)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Equations (5.2) and (5.3) concern the standard recursive algorithm s = 0; for i = 1:n, s = s + x_i, analyzed in the supplied order under the no-guard-digit addition model. They do not describe a compensated or pairwise variant. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: recursive-summation pseudocode; PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.1)-(5.3)]
numerical_model: The usual single-relative-error model (1.2) is declared invalid for machines lacking a guard digit in addition, and (5.1) is used instead. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: Section 5 opening and equation (5.1)]
The replacement model is componentwise: fl(x +/- y) = x(1 + alpha) +/- y(1 + beta), |alpha|, |beta| <= u. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.1)]
The model supplies separate perturbations for the accumulated prefix and the incoming term at each recursive addition. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.1) and (5.2)]

No concrete radix, precision, or IEEE rounding mode is specified for equations (5.1)-(5.3); only the abstract unit-roundoff bounds and absence of a guard digit are stated. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: Section 5 opening and equation (5.1)]
error_notions: E_n = S_hat_n - S_n is signed forward error; equations (5.3) and the subsequent estimates bound its scalar absolute value. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: definition of E_n; PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3)]
The bound is a computed-prefix or running-error bound because it contains S_hat_{k-1}, not the exact prefix S_{k-1}. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3)]

The direct bound also retains the individual input magnitudes |x_k|, unlike the standard-model bound (2.8). [PDF page 3 (printed 785), anchor: equation (2.8); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3)]
No relative-error conclusion is part of equations (5.1)-(5.3), and no nonzero-sum hypothesis is attached to them. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.1)-(5.3)]
norms: All displayed error measures are ordinary scalar absolute values. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.2) and (5.3)]
The sums of magnitudes in (5.3) are not identified as a named vector or matrix norm. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3) and its following sentence]
constants_and_indexing: The accumulated local-error sum and direct bound run from k = 2 through n. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.2) and (5.3)]
The direct bound uses S_hat_{k-1} and x_k; therefore its first prefix term is S_hat_1 = x_1. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3) and the following notice]
The looser computed-prefix bound has the explicit leading constant 3 and runs from k = 1 through n. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: sentence immediately after equation (5.3)]

Equation (5.3) has coefficient u, with no factor 1/(1-u); that denominator belongs to the cross-referenced standard-model bound (2.8). [PDF page 3 (printed 785), anchor: equation (2.8); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3)]

The unchanged gamma-bounds use gamma_m = m u/(1 - m u), including gamma_{n-1} and gamma_{n-i+1}. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: product convention after equation (2.2); PDF page 3 (printed 785), anchors: equations (2.5) and (2.6)]
higher_order_terms: Apart from the unbound-index problem in (5.2), equation (5.2) is printed as an equality and equation (5.3) as an inequality with no omitted higher-order term. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.2) and (5.3)]
Only the subsequent looser estimate introduces +O(u^2): 3u sum_{k=1}^n |S_hat_k| + O(u^2). [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: sentence immediately after equation (5.3)]

The unchanged bound (2.6) also has the first-order expansion (n - 1)u sum_i |x_i| + O(u^2). [PDF page 3 (printed 785), anchor: equation (2.6); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: statement that (2.6) is unchanged]
exceptional_values: Floating-point underflow is explicitly excluded by the paper's standing assumption. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: paragraph immediately after equation (1.2)]

The inspected model does not specify treatment of overflow, infinities, NaNs, subnormal results, or signed zeros. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: paragraph immediately after equation (1.2); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: Section 5 opening and equation (5.1)]
No positivity, common-sign, or noncancellation assumption is imposed on x_1,...,x_n for the recursive bounds. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: Section 2 opening and paragraph before equation (2.1)]

undebatable_constraints: The no-guard model perturbs x and y separately; it is not the single factor model fl(x + y) = (x + y)(1 + delta). [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.1)]
The error parameters satisfy inclusive bounds |alpha|, |beta| <= u and |alpha_k|, |beta_k| <= u. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.1) and (5.2)]
The source literally prints x_i beta_k in equation (5.2), while equation (5.3) prints |x_k|. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.2) and (5.3)]
The direct computed-prefix bound is |E_n| <= u sum_{k=2}^n (|S_hat_{k-1}| + |x_k|). [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3)]
The direct bound includes S_hat_1 = x_1 through the k = 2 term. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: sentence beginning 'Notice that (5.3)']
The looser bound has constant 3, index range k = 1,...,n, and an O(u^2) remainder. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: sentence immediately after equation (5.3)]
The signed error is computed minus exact: E_n = S_hat_n - S_n. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: definition of E_n]
No n-dependent smallness condition is printed alongside equations (5.2) or (5.3). [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.2) and (5.3)]
No-underflow is an inherited standing assumption. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: paragraph immediately after equation (1.2)]

ambiguities.issue: Equation (5.2) contains an unbound index: its summation variable is k, but the second local-error term is printed as x_i beta_k.
ambiguities.evidence: The literal display has x_i beta_k; the recursive step in (2.1) uses x_k, and the immediately following bound (5.3) uses |x_k|. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: equation (2.1); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.2) and (5.3)]
ambiguities.impact: A literal formal statement is not closed. Replacing x_i by x_k is the natural inferred correction, but that correction must be documented rather than attributed to the printed equation.

ambiguities.issue: The quantifier order and dependence of alpha and beta are conventional rather than formally stated.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (5.1) gives an equality and magnitude bounds but contains no explicit universal or existential quantifiers and does not state whether alpha and beta depend on the operands or operation sign. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.1)]
ambiguities.impact: The standard numerical-analysis reading is that a suitable pair exists for each performed operation; the passage does not support treating arbitrary bounded alpha and beta as producing fl(x +/- y), or treating one fixed pair as valid globally.

ambiguities.issue: The exact status of the inputs is not stated consistently at the same level of formality.
ambiguities.evidence: The abstract calls them floating-point numbers, while Section 2 calls x_1,...,x_n real numbers; no input-conversion errors are introduced and S_hat_1 = x_1 is used. [PDF page 1 (printed 783), anchor: Abstract; PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: Section 2 opening; PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: notice after equation (5.3)]
ambiguities.impact: The formulas should be read as operating on already-supplied data values without extra input-rounding terms, but the passage does not formally say whether arbitrary reals must be representable.

ambiguities.issue: The admissible range of n is not formally stated.
ambiguities.evidence: The algorithm is written for i = 1:n, while equations (5.2) and (5.3) sum from k = 2 to n; no empty-sum convention or explicit n >= 2 hypothesis is provided. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: recursive-summation pseudocode; PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.2) and (5.3)]
ambiguities.impact: For a formal contract, either restrict to n >= 2 or separately declare the empty-sum convention for n = 1; the paper does not choose explicitly.

ambiguities.issue: The scope and scaling of O(u^2) are unstated.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper writes 3u sum_{k=1}^n |S_hat_k| + O(u^2), and equation (2.6) also uses O(u^2), without specifying the hidden coefficient, its dimensional scale, or whether it is uniform in n and the data. [PDF page 3 (printed 785), anchor: equation (2.6); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: sentence immediately after equation (5.3)]
ambiguities.impact: Only the displayed first-order coefficient and index structure are fixed; a formal higher-order bound cannot be recovered without adding assumptions or an explicit remainder.

ambiguities.issue: The gamma convention is displayed without an explicit smallness hypothesis.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper defines gamma_m = m u/(1 - m u) after equation (2.2), but does not explicitly state m u < 1 there; Section 5 says the gamma-based bounds (2.5) and (2.6) are unchanged. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: product convention after equation (2.2); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: paragraph between equations (5.1) and (5.2)]
ambiguities.impact: A positive finite gamma-bound normally requires m u < 1, but that condition is inherited only implicitly and is not needed for the direct bound (5.3).

ambiguities.issue: The no-guard model does not identify a radix, precision, rounding mode, or behavior for overflow and nonreal exceptional values.
ambiguities.evidence: Section 5 supplies only the componentwise unit-roundoff model and a Cray motivation; the standing context explicitly addresses underflow but not the other cases. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: paragraph after equation (1.2); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: Section 5 opening and equation (5.1)]
ambiguities.impact: IEEE-specific behavior, round-to-nearest, overflow safety, and NaN or infinity semantics must not be added to the contract.

contract_plain_english: For recursive summation on arithmetic without a guard digit in addition, each addition or subtraction is modeled componentwise as fl(x +/- y) = x(1 + alpha) +/- y(1 + beta), with both error magnitudes at most u. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.1)] The exact sum is S_n, the recursively computed sum is S_hat_n, and the signed forward error is E_n = S_hat_n - S_n. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: Section 2 opening and definition of E_n] Equation (5.2) literally accumulates S_hat_{k-1} alpha_k + x_i beta_k, but i is unbound; applying the model to the kth recursion and comparing with (5.3) indicates that x_k beta_k was probably intended. [PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: equation (2.1); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchors: equations (5.2) and (5.3)] The unambiguous displayed bound is |E_n| <= u sum_{k=2}^n (|S_hat_{k-1}| + |x_k|), and it is further bounded by 3u sum_{k=1}^n |S_hat_k| + O(u^2). [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3) and its following sentence] This bound uses computed prefixes, includes S_hat_1 = x_1, and carries no relative-error or nonzero-sum requirement. [PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: equation (5.3) and the following notice] The cross-referenced gamma-bounds (2.5) and (2.6) remain unchanged after separating the x_1 and x_2 theta terms, and no underflow is allowed. [PDF page 3 (printed 785), anchors: equations (2.5) and (2.6); PDF page 11 (printed 793), anchor: paragraph between equations (5.1) and (5.2); PDF page 2 (printed 784), anchor: paragraph after equation (1.2)] Source PDF: :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/georgiosalexandrosgeorgantzas/GitHub/lean-fp-analysis/paper_bencmark/reference_papers/P01_THE ACCURACY OF FLOATING POINT SUMMATION.pdf" purpose="source"}
